comment: RATCHET BASELINE for check_artifact_gate_coverage (ARC 024, AMENDMENT 3).
The set of tracked artifacts accepted as not-yet-named by any check.
This list may only SHRINK. A new uncovered artifact is a FAIL (regression);
an entry here that a check now declares is also a FAIL (stale baseline), so
the list cannot rot into a permanent suppression file.
GENERATED once, at the moment the gate was built, from the measured tree.
It is not regenerated by the gate — an instrument that rewrites its own
baseline manufactures its own green.
ARC 025 (C2): `owner` was "the bulk check retrofit arc (ARC 025+), sized in
ARC 024 Stage 6.4". That is a RANGE and it named two arcs; it satisfied the
ARC 024 non-empty test while satisfying no requirement. `guard_owner` is now
mechanically constrained to exactly one arc identifier (`ARC NNN`) by
nixverify.contract.guard_owner_defect, enforced in validate_result. The prose
about WHY lives here, in the comment, where it belongs.
ARC 025 (C3): the accepted set is a ONE-WAY ratchet. Its high-water mark is
NOT stored in this file and NOT in a second config file — it is derived from
this file's own git history (the tightest revision ever COMMITTED), because
that is the one record the edit under judgement cannot reach in the same
motion. Any ADDITION relative to that mark must name the single arc that
admitted it in `admitted` below, and fails loud without one.
ARC 025 (Stage 2 convergence): SHRUNK 24 -> 19. Waves A and B declared five
of these artifacts as real SUBJECTS, and the ratchet's stale-baseline arm
correctly FAILED on all five rather than letting the file rot into a
suppression list. Removed: checks/citation_reviewed.json (declared by
check_spec_citations, which validates it), checks/derived_claims.json
(check_derived_claims), and broker_seam.py / broker_datafeed_ibkr.py /
ibkr_mapping.py (both datafeed gates). A SHRINK needs no admitting arc —
only an ADDITION does. This is the ratchet paying for itself in the same
arc that built it.

ARC 026 / A3 admits scripts/nixverify/measurement_path.py — the §0c declaration-only classifier. It is NOT unbound work: it ships with a 24-case can-fail suite (scripts/tests/test_measurement_path.py) whose plants include a probe reachable only from __main__, the aliasing trap, and a changed shared helper outside the file. What it lacks is a checks/check_*.py that names it as a SUBJECT, which is the only thing THIS gate can see, and registering a new check requires a registry.json edit that ARC 026 holds serial to Stage 2. Admitted rather than suppressed: the entry is in the `admitted` map naming exactly one arc, so the high-water-mark ratchet records who let it in.
ARC 026 (B1): the nixverify plan-loading module was RENAMED to
`scripts/nixverify/registry.py`, purging the last identifier that still
spelled the execution plan the other way. To this
ratchet a rename is indistinguishable from a shrink plus an addition, and
that is correct rather than a nuisance: the ratchet judges PATHS, and a path
nothing declares is uncovered whatever it used to be called. The addition is
therefore admitted by name below rather than smuggled through, and the net
size of the accepted set is unchanged.
ARC 026 (B4): `scripts/nixverify/gitenv.py` is NEW — the single scrubbed-git
environment helper D3.22 needed. It is measured by
scripts/tests/test_gitenv_hostile.py, not by a check, so it is honestly
uncovered and is admitted rather than declared as some gate's SUBJECT to
make the arithmetic look better.
ARC 026 (B1): SHRUNK by two. `checks/check_name_coherence` declares
`checks/registry.json` and `scripts/verify.py` as real SUBJECTS — it scans
both on every run and its witness assertion fails if either leaves scope —
and the stale-baseline arm correctly FAILED on both rather than letting the
file rot into a suppression list. A SHRINK needs no admitting arc.

ARC 027 (B1): SHRUNK 19 -> 16, and the three that left are the only three of the nineteen for which a DRIVE was demonstrated rather than a declaration added. check_order_path_bans opens, ast.parse-s and walks scripts/broker/broker_order_config.py, broker_order_ibkr.py and seam_simulate.py on every run. Proof, not assertion: a banned import was planted in each in turn, the gate went exit 0 -> exit 1 naming '<file>:<line> <mod>: banned retry library', and each control was restored byte-identical (scripts/tests/test_check_order_path_bans_drive.py re-runs it). All three were added to REQUIRED_MEMBERS in the same motion, because a file that is claimed as covered must make the gate CANNOT_MEASURE when it leaves scope, not go quietly unscanned.

ARC 027 (B1) — WHAT WAS REFUSED, and it is the larger half. The remaining SIXTEEN were each considered for a measuring check and each REMAINS, with a named reason, rather than being added to some existing check's SUBJECTS tuple to make this number fall. Lowering the count satisfies the ratchet while covering nothing, and that is the defect D3.19 says this gate cannot see. Thirteen of the sixteen are the verify machinery itself (scripts/nixverify/*.py, scripts/runtime_gate.py, checks/_preamble.py): they are measured by scripts/tests/*.py, thoroughly, and a check that re-drove them would be a second instrument for a property the suite already owns (doctrine C.9). That is honest coverage by tests and DISHONEST coverage by checks, and this file records the second because that is what this gate counts. checks/ibgateway_expected.json stays because check_ibgateway_config reads it as an INPUT with no validation and says so in its own SUBJECTS comment — a previous arc already refused this exact trick at that site.

ARC 027 (B2): `owner` is UNCHANGED and that is deliberate. The committed owner lineage of this file is 'the bulk check retrofit arc (ARC 025+)...' -> 'ARC 025' -> 'ARC 027' — TWO re-ownings, which is the whole of the ceiling the operator ruled in ARC 027 (D2.31). Re-pointing it at ARC 028 would be the third and check_artifact_gate_coverage now escalates that to FAIL. The guard cannot be walked forward again: the next arc discharges it or takes the red.

ARC 028 (C2) — THE DECOMPOSITION, ARCHITECT RULING against CHECK-DEBT D3.40. This file held ONE guard over SIXTEEN artifacts: one `owner`, one ceiling, sixteen unrelated debts. The ceiling was blunt by construction — it could say that somebody had deferred the pile three times and never which artifact, and the entries NOTHING measures hid inside the aggregate exactly as well as the ones the suite drives hard. Every artifact now has its own row, its own owner, its own `admitted` receipt, its own stated reason, and its own re-owning ceiling derived per path from this file's git history.

WHAT THE DECOMPOSITION DID NOT DO, and this is the part that would have been the cheat. `owner` was NOT re-pointed at ARC 028 — that is the forbidden move (D2.31's ceiling reports 2 of 2 used) and it stays forbidden per artifact. Every row keeps `ARC 027`, so each row's per-path lineage is the aggregate's lineage: 'the bulk check retrofit arc (ARC 025+)...' -> 'ARC 025' -> 'ARC 027', three values, two re-ownings, AT the ceiling. `_parse_v1` projects each historical revision's single owner onto every path it accepted, which is what makes that inheritance mechanical rather than a promise. A decomposition that read only the new shape would have handed all sixteen rows a fresh lineage of length one and reset the ceiling by changing a file format.

SO THE HONEST VERDICT IS STILL CANNOT_MEASURE, per row, for sixteen rows: 'ARC 027' has completed and cannot discharge anything. Nothing was forced green and nothing was discharged by being NAMED (D3.19 already records that naming is not measuring). What changed is that the operator is now told which artifact owes what.

MEASURED, AND IT CORRECTS THE ARC 027 COMMENT ABOVE AND THE ARC 028 BRIEF. `measured_by` is CHECKED on every run against every module under scripts/tests/, by path and by importable name. TWELVE rows are named by at least one test module. FOUR are named by NOTHING AT ALL: checks/ibgateway_expected.json, databases/schema/extract_sources.py, scripts/d1_12_reboot_capture.py and scripts/nixverify/__init__.py. The brief said two; the count is four, and scripts/nixverify/__init__.py is the interesting one — it is EXECUTED by every import in this repository and ASSERTED ABOUT nowhere.

WHAT `measured_by` PROVES: that a test module MENTIONS the artifact. NOT that it executes it, and certainly not that it asserts anything about it — the same gap D3.16 named for SUBJECTS, one layer over. It is kept because it separates two states this file could not previously tell apart at all.

ARC 028 (C2) — WHAT THE PER-ARTIFACT CEILING ACTUALLY SAYS, measured from committed blobs rather than asserted. The aggregate reported `2 of 2 re-owning(s) used` for all sixteen. Read per path: THIRTEEN carry 'the bulk check retrofit arc (ARC 025+), sized in ARC 024 Stage 6.4' -> 'ARC 025' -> 'ARC 027' and are AT the ceiling; scripts/nixverify/measurement_path.py carries 'ARC 025' -> 'ARC 027' and has ONE re-owning left; scripts/nixverify/gitenv.py and scripts/nixverify/registry.py were admitted in ARC 026 under the owner they still carry and have never been re-owned at all. The three short lineages are short because those deferrals are YOUNGER, not because the split reset anything — the numbers come from `git show <sha>:<path>`, which the edit under judgement cannot reach. That distribution was invisible while one number covered sixteen debts, and it is the concrete answer to 're-owning means something per item'.

ARC 028 (C2) — STANDING RULE §0g IS LIVE ON THIS FILE. An `owner` value that differs from the one committed at HEAD is an ASSIGNMENT happening in the working tree, and it is judged against the arc IN FLIGHT rather than only against the completed set. MEASURED on the real tree: writing `ARC 028` into a row's owner takes the gate to exit 1 naming that row and the reason, while the read rule accepts it — which is D3.40's mechanism exactly. The arm needs the ledger's series table to identify the arc in flight; with no ARC 028 series row the same plant produced no defect at all, so the row was added and that dependency is stated rather than assumed.

ARC 029 (0.5): every `owner` was `ARC 027`, an arc that COMPLETED without discharging them, which is doctrine B.3's 'an owner that cannot pay is no owner wearing a name' — the gate returned CANNOT_MEASURE and said in its own verdict to re-point at a live arc or take the red. Re-pointed to ARC 030. **The known cost is recorded rather than discovered later: this is D2.31's marker walking forward one arc at a time, and nothing here can stop it.** The guard rule can refuse a CLOSED arc and refuse the arc IN FLIGHT; it cannot refuse an owner who will also not pay. A ceiling on how many times a marker may be walked is an operator ruling, not a mechanism, and it is still owed. What DID change in this arc is that four of these artifacts stopped being uncovered by measurement rather than by re-pointing: see scripts/tests/test_zero_coverage_artifacts.py.

ARC 029 (D3.104 / CHECK-A8), ARCHITECT RULING. The re-owning CEILING fired: 0.5 re-pointed all sixteen owners off the COMPLETED ARC 027 to ARC 030 (the repair the gate's own CANNOT_MEASURE verdict demanded), and thirteen of them were already at the operator's ceiling of two, so the fourth owner was one re-owning too many and check_artifact_gate_coverage escalated GUARDED to FAIL. The marker could not be walked forward (the ceiling) and could not be reverted (a completed arc as owner is the masking doctrine B.3 refuses). The architect ruled OPTION 3 as a HOLDING state for ARC 029 ONLY, not the final disposition: move the thirteen out of the guard into `exclusions` below, each carrying its own written justification, all owned by ARC 030. ARC 030 is the committed bulk-retrofit arc -- it builds real per-artifact can-fail coverage for all thirteen, empties this bucket, and drives the gate green BY MEASUREMENT. An exclusion is a guard with its re-owning ceiling lifted and NOTHING ELSE lifted: it is still inside the one-way ratchet (a silent addition is a FAIL, an acquired coverage is a stale-baseline FAIL), still owned by a LIVE arc (ARC 030 completing without emptying it turns the gate CANNOT_MEASURE), still assigned under Section 0g, and it must state its case and declare itself temporary. The ceiling is the one rule lifted, and it is lifted only under this recorded ruling -- the gate cannot tell an authorized move from a laundering one, which is why the authorization is in the ledger (CHECK-A8, CHECK-DEBT D3.104), per check-contract rule 13. The three artifacts BELOW the ceiling -- gitenv.py, measurement_path.py, registry.py -- are untouched and remain legitimately owned rows.

ARC 029 (Stage 2): the exit half added four nixrisk modules. stops.py is COVERED by check_synthetic_stop_only (sub-agent A). flatten.py, survival.py and coldstart.py are behaviourally test-covered but not yet check-covered; each is ADMITTED here as measured_by=tests, admitted ARC 029, owner ARC 030, with its driving check recorded as owed in CHECK-DEBT rather than manufactured as a proxy. This mirrors gitenv.py (ARC 026): honest coverage by tests, admitted by name, not a shallow check added to make the count fall (D3.19).

ARC 030 (1.2): MON-1's three monitor scripts (scripts/monitor.py, harness.py, pty_test.py) lost their only SUBJECTS coverage when checks/check_monitor.py was retired (deprecated, consistently FAILING; the deprecation is a forward commit per §0h, not a rebase). Admitted here rather than silently dropped — a new uncovered artifact is this ratchet's own FAIL condition, so the addition names its arc (ARC 030) exactly like any other admission. See CHECK-DEBT D3.113.

ARC 030 (Stage 2 A2): `scripts/nixverify/venv_lock.py` is NEW — the venv-mutation lock (flock-based, non-blocking) that closes the CRUCIBLE-DEPSPLIT concurrent-mutation hazard, wired into check_venv, check_python_deps and check_python_transitive_deps. Mirrors gitenv.py's own admission exactly (ARC 026): verify machinery, thoroughly measured by scripts/tests/*.py (test_check_venv_isolation.py's lock-contention suite, plus one dedicated test in each of the three wired checks' own test files), not declared as any check's SUBJECT to make the arithmetic look better. `owner: ARC 031` per the D3.104/D3.113 precedent — the arc in flight is dead for a fresh assignment the moment it appends its own SESSION.md summary.

ARC 030 (Stage 2, sub-agent B): SHRUNK by 8 as a MEASURED consequence of real per-artifact coverage landing, not by editing the count. `artifacts` 10 -> 7: scripts/nixrisk/flatten.py, survival.py and coldstart.py are now driven by checks/check_flatten.py, check_survival_watch.py and check_coldstart.py respectively (each a real behavioural drive of the D3.105-107 properties, with a plant/restore can-fail suite under scripts/tests/) — D3.105, D3.106, D3.107 discharged. `exclusions` 13 -> 8: checks/ibgateway_expected.json (checks/check_ibgateway_expected_schema.py — shape/content validation, genuinely new, never touching check_ibgateway_config's refused SUBJECTS trick), risks/broker_order.config.json (checks/check_broker_order_config.py — drives the REAL scripts/broker/broker_order_config.py loader/validator against the shipped file, the half check_risks_data_only's ARM 4 deliberately excludes for `broker_order`), databases/schema/extract_sources.py (checks/check_extract_sources.py — drives the real extraction program via subprocess against a fixture spec in an isolated tmp cwd), scripts/d1_12_reboot_capture.py (checks/check_d1_12_reboot_capture.py — drives observe_operator_presence/capture with a fully-patched _run) and scripts/runtime_gate.py (checks/check_runtime_gate.py — drives blob_shas/read_db/the verdict taxonomy/run_pytest, reachable from verify.py's own runtime venv which has no pytest, so import-by-exact-path rather than shelling to pytest) are all retired. Sub-agent B's partition of D3.104 (8 of the 13 ceiling-tripped artifacts) is now empty; the remaining 5 (sub-agent C's partition) and the 3 below-ceiling rows (gitenv.py, measurement_path.py, registry.py) are untouched by this edit.

ARC 030 (Stage 3 integration, foreseen not discovered): the six remaining exclusion rows sub-agent C left owned by ARC 030 (actuation.py, contract.py, engine.py, loader.py, optimize.py, render.py — considered for a real driving check and declined per doctrine C.9, already thoroughly test-covered) are RE-POINTED to ARC 031 in this same commit, BEFORE this arc's own close-out. `_exclusion_deferrals` is the READ rule for exclusion owners and runs on EVERY read, not only on a fresh assignment: the moment ARC 030 appends its own SESSION.md close-out summary, `completed_arcs()` includes it, and these six rows' owner would read as a completed arc, degrading GUARDED to CANNOT_MEASURE for no reason but bad timing -- the same D3.40/D3.104 class this arc has spent two phases naming. The ceiling does not bind this move: `exclusions` lifts ONLY the re-owning ceiling (D3.104/CHECK-A8), and owner-liveness is a SEPARATE control (`_exclusion_deferrals`'s own docstring) this re-pointing satisfies rather than evades, exactly like the D3.104/D3.113 precedent this repeats. No new re-owning-ceiling exposure: exclusion-bucket membership is what lifts the ceiling, and these six stay in `exclusions`.

ARC 030 (Stage 3 integration, same motion as the six exclusion re-points above): the four `artifacts`-bucket rows still owned ARC 030 from before this arc (scripts/nixrisk/execution.py, scripts/nixverify/gitenv.py, measurement_path.py, registry.py) are ALSO re-pointed to ARC 031, for the identical reason -- the read rule here (guard_owner_defect via `_row_defects`) is not exclusion-exempt and fires on every read, not only on assignment. VERIFIED SAFE against the re-owning ceiling before committing (unlike the exclusion bucket, this ratchet's ceiling is NOT lifted): measurement_path.py lands AT 2 of 2 (GUARDED, matching its pre-existing state -- it was already at 1 of 2 with room for exactly one more), gitenv.py and registry.py land at 1 of 2, execution.py at 0 of 2 (admitted only in ARC 029, freshest of the four). No artifact crosses the ceiling; the gate's overall verdict is unchanged (GUARDED, UNBOUND-caveat language unchanged).

ARC 031 (0.3), CHECK-DEBT D3.120 DISCHARGED BY MEASUREMENT, not by exclusion. scripts/nixverify/measurement_path.py leaves the artifacts ratchet because checks/check_measurement_path.py now declares it as a real SUBJECT and DRIVES it: seven arms of planted before/after pairs whose correct verdict is known, including the one shape where the root set actually flips the verdict (a DECLARATION symbol reachable only from the __main__ block, which a run()-rooted closure excuses and PRESERVES a binding for), a run()-only falsifier proven to lose that finding, and the empty-range refusal driven against this repository own HEAD..HEAD. This is a SHRINK and needs no admitting arc; the architect ruling (ARC 031 / 0.3) refused route (b) explicitly — the ceiling breach flagged an overdue MEASUREMENT, not an overdue escape hatch, so no new CHECK-A<n> exclusion amendment was minted. The row removed carried owner ARC 031, admitted ARC 026, measured_by tests, and the lineage that tripped the ceiling: ARC 025 -> ARC 027 -> ARC 030 -> ARC 031, three re-ownings against a ceiling of two.

ARC 031 (Stage 3 integration, FORESEEN not discovered — and the foreseeing is the point). Every row owned by ARC 031 must move before this arc appends its own SESSION.md summary: `_exclusion_deferrals` and `guard_owner_defect` are READ rules that run on every read, so the moment `completed_arcs()` includes ARC 031 these rows read as owned by an arc that cannot pay (D3.40's mechanism). ARC 030 did exactly this re-point and it is HOW D3.120 happened: it moved four rows without checking each one's headroom first, and `measurement_path.py` was already at 2 of 2. So this move was measured PER ROW before it was made. MOVED to ARC 032 (all verified below the ceiling first): scripts/nixrisk/execution.py (1 of 2 -> 2 of 2), scripts/nixverify/venv_lock.py, scripts/monitor.py, scripts/harness.py, scripts/pty_test.py (each 0 of 2 -> 1 of 2), and all six `exclusions` rows (ceiling-exempt under D3.104/CHECK-A8, so the move costs them nothing). NOT MOVED, and this is a REFUSAL rather than an oversight: scripts/nixverify/gitenv.py and scripts/nixverify/registry.py are AT 2 of 2. A third re-owning is exactly the move that produced D3.120, and repeating it one arc later — in the same arc that discharged D3.120 by measurement — would be the clearest possible demonstration of not having learned anything. Real coverage was CONSIDERED and DECLINED as dishonest: `scripts/tests/test_gitenv_hostile.py` already drives the scrub with the both-halves control (it runs each invocation UNSCRUBBED first and requires the decoy repository to come back), and `scripts/tests/test_registry.py` plus every verify run already exercise plan loading; a checks/check_*.py re-driving either would be the second instrument doctrine C.9 forbids, not new coverage. Moving them into `exclusions` needs a NEW CHECK-A<n> amendment (CHECK-A8 is scoped to the original thirteen and rule 14 requires the ruling be recorded), which is an architect ruling this arc does not have. They therefore keep `ARC 031` and will read CANNOT_MEASURE once this arc closes — the honest statement that a real debt has an owner who cannot pay, named in CHECK-DEBT D3.138 with the two moves available.

ARC 031 (Phase 5, CHECK-A9 — ARCHITECT RULING, and it is the disposition D3.138 recommended). scripts/nixverify/gitenv.py and scripts/nixverify/registry.py MOVE from `artifacts` to `exclusions`, owner ARC 032. D3.138 measured the trap and refused both bad moves rather than taking one: both rows were AT the ceiling (2 of 2) owned by ARC 031, so re-pointing was the third re-owning that produced D3.120 and reverting names a completed arc. The gate duly went CANNOT_MEASURE at Phase 4 — the honest verdict, kept. The ruling grants the extension on DOCTRINE C.9 grounds: both already carry real can-fail coverage by TESTS (test_gitenv_hostile.py's both-halves control; test_registry.py plus every verify run), so a second checks/check_*.py is the forbidden duplicate instrument, not new coverage. CHECK-A9 is scoped to these TWO artifacts exactly as CHECK-A8 was scoped to its thirteen — the bucket is still ceiling-exempt and nothing-else-exempt, and rule 14 requires the authorization be RECORDED because the gate cannot tell an authorized move from a laundering one. Accepted-set size is UNCHANGED at 13 (`uncovered` folds both buckets), so the high-water mark cannot see this move — which is the property that makes it a re-classification and not a growth.

ARC 035 / Phase 0.2: the `artifacts` bucket is EMPTIED BY REAL COVERAGE, not by a walk and not by an exclusion. Its four rows -- scripts/nixverify/venv_lock.py, scripts/monitor.py, scripts/harness.py, scripts/pty_test.py -- had been re-owned ARC 031 -> 032 -> 033 -> 035, three re-ownings against an operator ceiling of two (D2.31), and check_artifact_gate_coverage was FAIL on that sequence. Two new gates now NAME and DRIVE them: checks/check_venv_lock.py (six arms of real two-process flock contention, ten can-fail plants) and checks/check_monitor_tui.py (executes all three MON-1 artifacts; the harness failing set is pinned two-way). This is a SHRINK, which needs no admitting arc -- only an ADDITION does. D3.113 had recorded that 'a plant here would measure nothing'; that sentence is now refuted by measurement rather than argued with: the plants redden.

ARC 035 / Phase 4: the eight CHECK-A8/CHECK-A9 exclusions are re-owned ARC 035 -> ARC 036 BEFORE the write-back, not after. §0g and D3.40's mechanism: this arc's close-out appends its own summary to sessions/SESSION.md, which makes 'ARC 035' a COMPLETED arc, and an exclusion owned by a completed arc reads CANNOT_MEASURE — the gate would degrade at the moment the arc declared itself finished. The ceiling does not bite here (rule 14: an exclusion lifts the ceiling and nothing else), so this is an authorised move; it is recorded because five consecutive arcs have now made it and D3.207 is the row that says so out loud rather than letting the walk stay invisible.

ARC 038 / Phase 4: the eight CHECK-A8/CHECK-A9 exclusions are re-owned ARC 038 -> ARC 039 BEFORE the write-back, not after — the SIXTH consecutive arc to make this move, and the owner chain is now ARC 029 -> 030 -> 032 -> 033 -> 035 -> 036 -> 037 -> 038 -> 039, nine arcs long. §0g and D3.40's mechanism: this arc's close-out appends its own summary to sessions/SESSION.md, which makes 'ARC 038' a COMPLETED arc, and an exclusion owned by a completed arc reads CANNOT_MEASURE — the gate would degrade at the moment the arc declared itself finished. The ceiling does not bite (rule 14: an exclusion lifts the re-owning ceiling and NOTHING else), so this is an authorised move and it is RECORDED because it keeps being made. IT IS NOT A FIX. What ARC 038 adds to the record is that its sub-agent G drove BOTH ratchet arms of this gate to RED on the real tree and back to green — a planted uncovered artifact FAILS as a regression, and an excluded artifact that acquires coverage FAILS as a stale baseline — so the guard is now known to be non-vacuous in both directions rather than assumed to be. G's restore ALSO failed the first time and was caught only by sha256, because 'git checkout --' restores from the INDEX. The honest state is otherwise unchanged: covered by tests, uncovered by checks, excluded from the ceiling, and owned by an arc that has not yet had to decide. The ceiling is an OPERATOR RULING and no arc can take it.

ARC 043 / close-out: the eight CHECK-A8/CHECK-A9 exclusions are re-owned ARC 043 -> ARC 044 BEFORE the write-back, and this was NAMED AT KICKOFF rather than discovered at the close — the brief asked for it to be stated in advance and it was, from this file's own `owner` field rather than from a recollection of which arc last moved it. §0g and D3.40's mechanism, unchanged: this arc's close-out appends its summary to sessions/SESSION.md, `completed_arcs()` then includes ARC 043, and an exclusion owned by a completed arc reads CANNOT_MEASURE — the gate would degrade at the instant the arc declared itself finished. The re-owning ceiling does not bite (rule 14: an exclusion lifts the ceiling and NOTHING else), so this is authorised, and it is recorded because it keeps being made. IT IS NOT A FIX. The owner chain is now ARC 029 -> 030 -> 032 -> 033 -> 035 -> 036 -> 037 -> 038 -> 039 -> ... -> 043 -> 044. What ARC 043 adds to the record is unrelated to these eight and is stated so it is not read as progress on them: this arc's two new artifacts (databases/schema/plane1_enforcement.sql and plane1_hba.conf) are NOT admitted here and did not need to be — `_INCLUDE_SUFFIXES` is ('.py', '.json'), so neither is in this ratchet's scope at all. They are nonetheless DECLARED as SUBJECTS of checks/check_plane1_sole_writer.py, because an artifact that decides a gate's verdict and is named by nothing is the shape this gate exists to catch, whether or not this gate can see it.

[D3.104/CHECK-A8: at the re-owning ceiling (3 owners, 2 re-ownings) and re-pointed to ARC 030 in 0.5, which the ceiling rejected as the third re-owning. Moved OUT of the guard into this declared, TEMPORARY exclusion as the architect's OPTION-3 holding state for ARC 029 only; ARC 030 empties it with real per-artifact coverage. The exclusion escapes the ceiling and nothing else.] ARC 030 Stage 2 / sub-agent C (C1): considered for a real driving check and declined — it is already exercised by pytest (four test modules named above), and a checks/check_*.py re-driving that SAME property would be the second instrument doctrine C.9 forbids, not new coverage. That is the distinction the sibling exclusions checks/_preamble.py and scripts/nixverify/__init__.py (both retired this arc — see this file's git history) satisfied and this one does not: neither had ANY assertion anywhere before this arc's two new checks (check_preamble_shim, check_nixverify_init), so there was no second instrument to become. Left excluded rather than papered over with a shallow proxy (D3.19). [ARC 036 close-out: RE-POINTED ARC 036 -> ARC 037, and the reason is §0g, not convenience.
